threat_model: planner/LLM assumed compromised; tool output, memory, MCP, retrieved content assumed hostile

findings.title: fs.search 'glob' argument bypasses workspace confinement -> arbitrary file read
findings.precondition: agent granted fs.search (default: coder, analyst); compromised planner emits crafted glob
findings.attack: fs.search(pattern='.', glob='../../outside/*') -> reads BOSSMAN_TEST_SECRET_9F31A7 two levels above workspace
findings.actual: ctx.workdir.rglob(glob) follows '../' with no _resolve check; matching lines returned to model
findings.root_cause: fs_search never calls _resolve on the glob; rglob accepts relative-parent patterns
findings.impact: arbitrary read of any file the core process can read (other agents' workspaces, source, config, container fs; host fs on local mode)

findings.title: fs.* root confinement by str.startswith allows sibling-directory escape
findings.precondition: sibling dir whose name shares the workdir name prefix; agent can create one via fs.write
findings.trust_boundary: agent workdir root confinement / cross-agent isolation
findings.attack: workdir=/ws/coder; fs.read('../coder-secrets/s.txt') and fs.write('../coder-secrets/pwned.txt') both succeed
findings.root_cause: prefix string test instead of Path.relative_to/parents containment
findings.impact: cross-agent read/write when agent names share a prefix; write to arbitrary /ws/<workdir-prefix>* siblings

findings.title: media.probe applies no path validation (ffmpeg twin does)
findings.attack: media.probe(path='../../../../etc/passwd') -> ffprobe on out-of-workdir file; metadata/existence disclosure
findings.expected: reject absolute/.. paths like ffmpeg does
findings.root_cause: the _path_arg_ok discipline used by ffmpeg was not applied to probe
findings.impact: file-existence + media metadata oracle outside workdir

findings.title: http tool = full SSRF (model-controlled URL, no confirm, no host/scheme/redirect checks)
findings.attack: http(url='http://169.254.169.254/...') or loopback pivot to gateway/core admin ports
findings.expected: scheme allowlist, private-IP/metadata block, redirect cap, or approval
findings.actual: httpx.request(method, url, json, params) with zero validation; response written to assets and returned
findings.root_cause: tool ships with no egress policy
findings.impact: SSRF, internal service pivot, metadata theft when granted

findings.title: Project runner invokes tool handlers directly, bypassing agent grants + approvals; cmd kind is a real shell fed LLM-plan params
findings.precondition: POST /projects/{slug}/run (SCOPE_CHAT) on an approved project whose LLM plan selects a builtin/cmd tool
findings.attack: planner-authored plan params flow into REGISTRY[...].handler(t.params) with no grant/confirm/approval; cmd templates run via create_subprocess_shell(spec['cmd'].format(**shlex_quoted_params))
findings.expected: same grant + confirm + approval path as runner._call_tool
findings.actual: second dispatch path with no approval; builtins limited to ffmpeg/vision.describe by current registry, but lookup is by config string
findings.root_cause: projects pipeline reuses REGISTRY handlers without the runner's enforcement wrapper; shlex.quote is POSIX-only
findings.impact: consequential tools executed without approval; shell template injection surface if registry gains a template with model-controlled placeholder keys

findings.title: Retrieved memory injected as system role without untrusted marker; model-written facts read back unmarked
findings.surface: bossman-core context.py:build (retrieved block); command-center features/tools_facts.py (search/history not external_output)
findings.precondition: untrusted text reaches the context store (search.index tool) or a self-authored fact is recalled
findings.enforcement_layer: EXTERNAL_DATA_HEADER (applied to tool read/send output only)
findings.attack: content indexed via search.index / memory.fact.add is re-rendered into a system message (core) or returned without the untrusted-data header (CC facts), unlike tool output
findings.expected: all model-influenced / retrieved content carries the same untrusted-data framing as tool output
findings.actual: core retrieved block uses role=system with provenance label only; CC fact search/history/at_time omit external_output and omit source_kind in render
findings.root_cause: inconsistent application of the untrusted-data boundary across ingestion paths
findings.impact: indirect prompt injection / memory poisoning surface if any untrusted text is indexed

findings.title: exec/write tool results returned to model without untrusted-data header or ingest guard
findings.precondition: agent runs run/tests/git/ffmpeg/browser.click whose output carries attacker-controlled repo/network text
findings.enforcement_layer: EXTERNAL_DATA_HEADER + cybersec ingest_guard (skipped for exec/write rights)
findings.attack: output of `run` (stdout of README/curl inside sandbox) returns unmarked and un-inspected
findings.expected: same data framing for exec/write output that carries external content
findings.actual: header/guard gated on rights read/send; run/tests(exec), git(write), browser.click(write) bypass it
findings.root_cause: boundary keyed on tool 'rights' rather than on 'does this output contain external content'
findings.impact: weaker prompt-injection hygiene (the doc notes the header is probability-reduction, not a control)

findings.title: Gateway trusts client cloud-policy header (fail-open default); embeddings never checks; is_cloud() prefix mislabel creates audit hole
findings.precondition: a direct gateway client (bearer or loopback-unauth) that omits X-Bossman-Cloud-Allowed; or a capability alias routing to cloud
findings.enforcement_layer: router.resolve cloud drop (driven by a client header defaulting to '1'=allowed)
findings.attack: omit header -> cloud allowed; /v1/embeddings never passes cloud_allowed; capability-alias cloud calls recorded is_cloud=False so skip cloud_calls audit row
findings.expected: fail-closed default (deny cloud unless explicitly allowed) and audit of every cloud egress
findings.actual: default permissive; embeddings unchecked; audit row keyed on alias prefix, not on whether the route was actually cloud
findings.root_cause: the most important egress decision lives in a client-supplied header with a fail-open default; audit derives cloudness from the alias name not the resolved route
findings.impact: cloud egress by a non-Bossman client; incomplete 'every byte that left' audit. NOTE: for the compromised-planner path, never-agents are still blocked (llm.py sets header '0'); this is hardening + audit completeness

findings.title: command-center terminal.run mode=sandbox skips root confinement and bind-mounts arbitrary cwd RW, at auto effect
findings.precondition: agent granted terminal.run; docker runtime present
findings.enforcement_layer: allowed-roots check (explicitly skipped when mode=='sandbox') and engine ASK (auto in sandbox)
findings.attack: terminal.run(mode='sandbox', cmd='cat /work/...', cwd='/etc') -> effective_roots=[cwd], root check skipped, `-v /etc:/work` bind mount, decision 'auto' so no approval
findings.expected: cwd confined to allowed roots and consequential exec approved
findings.actual: sandbox path removes the root check and defaults non-DANGEROUS commands to auto
findings.root_cause: sandbox mode trusts model-supplied cwd as its own root and treats containerization as sufficient to drop approval
findings.impact: arbitrary host directory mounted RW into a container and operated on without approval

findings.title: command-center browser.open has no default URL allowlist and runs at auto effect
findings.enforcement_layer: BrowserPolicy.domain_allowed (returns True when allowed_domains empty = default)
findings.attack: browser.open('http://169.254.169.254/') or internal URL; auto navigate; page content then drives auto click/type
findings.expected: default-deny or allowlist for navigation targets
findings.actual: empty allowlist = allow anything; navigate/click/type all auto
findings.root_cause: allowlist defaults to permissive; policy built from agent.permissions['browser'] which is normally absent
findings.impact: SSRF-via-browser, indirect injection surface, unbounded navigation

findings.title: Cross-task/session hijack via model-supplied session_id (browser/terminal/opencode)
findings.precondition: two concurrent tasks; compromised planner supplies another task's session_id
findings.enforcement_layer: none (global session lookup by model-supplied id)
findings.attack: browser._session_for honors args['session_id'] with no ownership check; terminal.status/stdin/kill index mgr.sessions globally; opencode.send matches session_id ignoring run/task
findings.expected: session bound to the run/task that created it
findings.actual: global maps keyed only by id
findings.root_cause: no ownership binding between a live session and its task/run
findings.impact: one task drives another task's browser (post-human-login), terminal, or opencode worktree

findings.title: Review/verification gate returns PASS when worker echoes the criteria string (verification spoofing)
findings.precondition: review configured without reviewer_agent_id (deterministic path), or with a same-family reviewer model
findings.attack: worker answer 'I confirm: <criteria text> (nothing executed)' -> criteria.lower() in answer.lower() -> PASS with no external evidence; LLM path uses text.upper().startswith('PASS')
findings.expected: verdict grounded in fresh, independent external state, not in the reviewed text
findings.actual: substring-of-criteria => PASS; LLM verdict is self-reported prefix
findings.root_cause: verification derived from the artifact's own text rather than re-observed external state
findings.impact: false-green completion; task marked completed on model self-report

findings.title: Approval not bound to args hash; MCP tool re-register by name swaps approved implementation at resume
findings.precondition: an ASK'd tool call is parked; before resume, POST /mcp/runtime/servers/{ref}/refresh re-registers mcp:<server>:<tool> with a new handler/spec
findings.trust_boundary: approved action identity == executed action identity
findings.enforcement_layer: approval binds approval_id -> tool_calls(run,call_id) by NAME; args_hash computed and stored but never compared
findings.attack: human approves preview of tool X; refresh re-registers X's handler; resume does TOOLS.get(name) -> executes new implementation
findings.expected: resume verifies the stored args_hash AND the tool implementation identity equal what was approved
findings.actual: args_hash is write-only (no reader); spec re-resolved by name at resume; ToolRegistry.register silently overwrites on name collision
findings.root_cause: approval identity is a name+call_id, not a content hash of (tool-impl, args)
findings.impact: approved-by-name / executed-different-impl; also name-collision overwrite from a second MCP server

findings.title: Hostile MCP server tool description/input_schema injected unfiltered into the model's tool catalogue
findings.precondition: a malicious/compromised MCP server is connected (owner adds it; command allowlist absent)
findings.trust_boundary: MCP content is data, must not become authority
findings.enforcement_layer: none on descriptions/schemas (results do get EXTERNAL_DATA_HEADER)
findings.attack: server returns tool description containing instructions; description[:900] inserted verbatim into the schema the model sees, persisted to mcp_tools, reloaded at boot
findings.expected: MCP-authored metadata treated as untrusted data, not merged into the instruction surface
findings.actual: verbatim description/schema in the model's tool list; structured result content passed unbounded/unredacted into ToolResult.data
findings.root_cause: MCP metadata trusted like first-party tool definitions
findings.impact: prompt injection via tool catalogue; also POST /api/mcp/servers accepts arbitrary argv command with no allowlist (owner-gated local code exec)

findings.title: Self-asserted approval flags and unbound approvals on owner HTTP routes
findings.surface: command-center features/terminal.py:86-100, features/browser.py:126, features/snapshot.py:556-565, features/nl_orchestra.py:164-171, api.py PATCH /agents
findings.precondition: holder of the single owner token (all CC routes are owner-token gated)
findings.enforcement_layer: approvals table (not consulted on these paths)
findings.attack: terminal.run body approved:true skips approval row (incl system_admin); browser act actor='human' defeats ASK+takeover; snapshot restore checks kind not snapshot_id; orchestras/confirm trusts client 'valid'; PATCH /agents rewrites permissions with no approval
findings.expected: approval decisions verified against the approvals table and bound to the exact target
findings.actual: client-asserted flags trusted; approvals bound to kind not id
findings.root_cause: UI convenience flags trusted as authority on server side
findings.impact: owner-authority integrity / UI-spoofing; not a privilege escalation given single-token model, but violates approval-before-effect

findings.title: Router cloud gating defaults to allow; force_model_id and local-mislabel bypass policy
findings.precondition: task without cloud_budget meta; or fork with meta.force_model_id; or a cloud model mislabeled kind=local
findings.attack: no meta -> cloud_allowed True; meta.force_model_id returns any model with no cloud/price/capability check; a cloud model with DB kind=local passes 'cloud disabled' filter
findings.expected: fail-closed cloud gating and policy-checked model override
findings.actual: permissive default, unchecked override, label-driven gate
findings.root_cause: cloud gating is advisory (budget-derived) with no global deny; override bypasses it

findings.title: Authenticated SSRF (discovery extra_urls) and path traversal (taskxchange result)
findings.enforcement_layer: none (discovery does not use plugin_security.validate_url; app_id not validated vs known_apps)
findings.attack: POST /api/models/discover extra_urls=['http://169.254.169.254/...']; GET /taskxchange/result/%2e%2e%2f.../{task_id} reads/creates dirs outside APPS_DIR
findings.expected: URL validation; app_id validated against known_apps before path join
findings.actual: arbitrary URL fetched and returned; traversal-based mkdir + read of .../completed/<task_id>.json
findings.root_cause: missing validation on owner-only maintenance routes
findings.impact: SSRF and limited traversal read/mkdir under owner authority

findings.title: Dead / unwired security code (exists but not enforced)
findings.surface: command-center bcc/v2/permissions.py, v2/code_index.py:_within, bcc/context_os/*, bcc/secrets.py:mask_enc; bossman-core bossman/capabilities.py, sandbox/secrets.py, toolkit/analysis.py, toolkit/fileintel.py
findings.expected: security modules that exist are wired into production paths
findings.actual: PermissionPolicy.safe_default() deny-list (*.env/id_rsa/wallet) has no importer; code_index._within defined-never-called so iter_files indexes symlink targets outside root; context_os injectors never attached; Secret Broker (sandbox/secrets.py) never instantiated; capabilities.py advisory-only; analysis.run/file.parse/artifact.create never registered in production REGISTRY; mask_enc no callers
findings.impact: protections assumed but not enforced; classify DEAD_UNWIRED / TEST_ONLY
